subtitle: Lesson 19 · Core ITIL 4 Practices: Request, Knowledge & Service Level

code:
Purpose: support the agreed quality of a service by
handling all predefined, user-initiated service
requests in an effective, user-friendly manner.

Nothing is broken. The service works as designed --
the user just needs it to do one of its jobs.
caption: A service request is a planned ask, not an unplanned break.

code:
Incident:                       Service request:
Unplanned interruption          Planned, expected ask
Something is wrong              Nothing is wrong
"Fix this"                      "Do this for me"
E.g. app server crashed         E.g. new laptop, access, reset
caption: Same ticket queue, a completely different kind of work.

steps.label: Information needed
steps.sub: captured up front, so nobody has to guess what's missing

steps.label: Approval chain
steps.sub: who signs off, decided when the request was designed, not case by case

steps.label: Fulfillment steps
steps.sub: a known workflow instead of improvising a process each time

code:
Service catalog: a menu of what can be requested,
with details (model, cost center, approver) captured
at the point of request.

Some requests: built-in approval step (manager,
security).
Other requests: pre-approved -- risk judged low
enough at design time -- fulfill automatically.
caption: The catalog is the front door; approval is built into the workflow.

subtitle: What the organization already knows, made fast to find.
